root_cause.text: The Rockchip rkcif MIPI register accessor functions used incorrect `>` bounds checks on array indices (`block`, `id`, and `index`), allowing an off-by-one access one element past the end of `match_data->mipi->blocks`, `regs`, and `regs_id` arrays.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly changes `WARN_ON_ONCE(block > ...)`, `WARN_ON_ONCE(id > ...)`, and `WARN_ON_ONCE(index > ...)` to `>= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and the commit message states this was done “to avoid accessing one element beyond the end of the arrays.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Rockchip rkcif MIPI register accessor functions used incorrect `>` bounds checks on array indices (`block`, `id`, and `index`), allowing an off-by-one access one element past the end of `match_data->mipi->blocks`, `regs`, and `regs_id` arrays.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch explicitly changes `WARN_ON_ONCE(block > ...)`, `WARN_ON_ONCE(id > ...)`, and `WARN_ON_ONCE(index > ...)` to `>= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and the commit message states this was done “to avoid accessing one element beyond the end of the arrays.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace hardcoded MIPI register bounds checks with array-size based validation to prevent invalid table access.
intent_record.what: The bounds checks in rkcif_mipi_get_reg() were changed from comparing block against a fixed arithmetic limit and index against RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX to using ARRAY_SIZE() on rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks and rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs, respectively. The return behavior on failed checks remains the same.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now validates the block and register index against the actual sizes of the per-match-data tables instead of hardcoded maximum constants. This makes out-of-range access prevention align with the active hardware description and avoids indexing past the ends of the blocks/regs arrays.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bounds validation in rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg() by checking indices against the actual array sizes to prevent out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: The three bounds checks in rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg() were changed from comparisons against fixed maximum constants using '>' to comparisons against the corresponding array sizes using '>='. Specifically, the checks now validate 'block' against rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks, 'id' against rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id, and 'index' against rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id[id].
intent_record.how: This makes the function reject out-of-range indices at the exact array boundary and ties validation to the actual data structure sizes instead of hard-coded limits. It prevents potential out-of-bounds access when selecting the MIPI block, register ID table, or per-ID register entry, returning RKCIF_REGISTER_NOTSUPPORTED earlier for invalid inputs.

grouping_result.intent: Fix bounds validation in rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg() by checking indices against the actual array sizes to prevent out-of-bounds access.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix bounds validation in rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg() by replacing hardcoded MIPI register checks with actual array-size validation to prevent out-of-bounds access.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the reported off-by-one out-of-bounds issue in the Rockchip rkcif MIPI register accessor by replacing incorrect bounds checks with proper array-size validation for the affected indices.

candidates.rationale: This check uses a strict '>' comparison, so an index equal to the array size can still pass and later access one element past the end of match_data->mipi->blocks.
Using '>' here allows index values equal to the maximum to be treated as valid, which can lead to an out-of-bounds access in the registers table.
This off-by-one bounds check can admit block == array_size, enabling access past the end of match_data->mipi->blocks.
The incorrect strict bound lets id values equal to the limit through, which can index one past the end of the regs_id array.
This off-by-one comparison can permit index == max, leading to an out-of-bounds read from the regs array.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check uses '>' instead of '>=' for the block index, allowing an off-by-one value equal to the array size to pass and later access one element past the end of match_data->mipi->blocks.
This strict upper-bound check incorrectly permits id == RKCIF_ID_MAX, which can index one element past the end of the regs_id array.
This comparison allows index values equal to the maximum, creating an off-by-one out-of-bounds access risk in the registers table.
This check uses '>' rather than '>=' for the register index, which can admit index == max and cause an out-of-bounds read from the regs array.
